## Excluded GLM-5.3-Flash attempt

GLM-5.3-Flash is excluded from the comparative harness results because the
available Fireworks-backed inference did not produce a usable benchmark
condition. The problem was not a low task score or provider rate limiting. The
recorded trajectories show extreme repetitive behavior and token consumption
that is inconsistent with the other model runs on the same tasks
[@pa1GlmBenchmarkData].

The clearest example is the Codex run on
`effect-sse-httpapi-streaming`. It reached **780,117,872 input tokens**, of
which **775,819,264 were cached-input tokens**, and **2,355 agent steps** before
the three-hour timeout. Within that trajectory, the exact command
`rg -n "Schema.Simplify" packages/effect/src/Schema.ts` was issued **1,869
times**. On the same task and harness, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash used 32,137,444
cached-input tokens and 277 steps, while Kimi K3 used 19,317,706 cached-input
tokens and 161 steps. A separate Pi GLM run on `scriggo-method-declarations`
showed the same failure pattern: 302,913,536 cached-input tokens and 1,301
steps before timeout, including 743 repetitions of the same probe command
[@pa1GlmBenchmarkData].

These runs consumed most of the remaining experiment budget without yielding a
complete comparable GLM matrix [@pa1GlmExclusion]. Because no alternative
GLM-5.3-Flash provider was available, the study could not determine whether the
pathological behavior originated in the model itself or in the Fireworks
serving implementation. The Fireworks-backed GLM condition is therefore treated
as an inference failure, not as a valid harness-performance observation. The
raw data is retained for transparency but excluded from the cross-harness
performance and cost analysis.
